boss.hex.name: Hex Warden
boss.hex.description: Arcane hexagonal boss: spiked crystal shell around a slowly rotating facet plate, a radial-gradient soul core, and angry ember eyes inside an orbit ring. Enraged variant goes blood-red, gold-cored, and grows horns.

enraged.description: Blood shell, gold core, bone horns — phase-two look built from the same parts.

idle.description: facet plate spins slowly, core pulses, aura breathes

char.dot.name: Dot
char.dot.description: Round frost-blue starter character: glowing aura, circular body with a highlight, shared library face. Bobs gently at idle.

enemy.grunt.name: Grunt
enemy.grunt.description: Armored walker: dark-plum torso, steel pauldrons, ember scarf, gold visor eye, swinging fists. The Cellspire grunt rebuilt with an actual silhouette.

walk.description: fist pump + head sway + body bob

enemy.imp.name: Imp
enemy.imp.description: Small aggressive melee chaser: round crimson body, bone horns, whipping tail, gold eyes. Elite variant turns arcane, grows a third eye and 25% size.

elite.description: Arcane recolor + third eye + 1.25× scale. A themed variant, not just a tint.

fx.burst.name: Death burst
fx.burst.description: Radial debris burst for kills and pickups: seeded gold shard scatter over an ember core. Port of Cellspire's Glob.burst verb.

play.description: shards fly out (uniform expand) and fade

fx.impact.name: Impact flash
fx.impact.description: Hit feedback: a four-point bone sliver star popping over a frost flash. Port of Cellspire's Glob.impact verb.

fx.muzzle.name: Muzzle flash
fx.muzzle.description: Ranged-attack muzzle cone: gold outer wedge, ember inner wedge, anchored at the barrel (left edge) so it points +x. Port of Cellspire's Glob.muzzle verb.

fx.ring.name: AoE ring
fx.ring.description: Expanding area-of-effect telegraph ring with a soft inner wash. Port of Cellspire's Glob.ring verb; tintable by swapping the fill token.

fx.slash.name: Slash arc
fx.slash.description: Melee slash feedback: a bone arc blade with a frost leading edge, fading out. Port of Cellspire's Glob.slash verb as a document.

icon.boomerang.name: Boomerang icon
icon.boomerang.description: UI slot icon: rounded tile + frost rim + the actual weapon.boomerang document composed via `use` — no second hand-drawn copy. Evolved variant swaps the rim to gold and adds a spark.

evolved.description: Gold rim + corner spark; the `_evo` twin, derived instead of re-drawn.

lib.face.name: Face
lib.face.description: Shared friendly face: two ink eyes and soft blush cheeks. Composed into characters via `use` so every character shares one face definition.

pickup.chest.name: Treasure chest
pickup.chest.description: Timber chest with iron bands, gold latch and a warm glow; the lid rattles. Cursed variant recolors to arcane wood with soul-lit eyes peeking from under the lid.

cursed.description: Arcane wood, soul latch, glowing eyes in the gap — same parts, darker story.

ss.char.blok.name: Blok
ss.char.blok.description: Sealed survivor in a squared-off shell with a riveted seam — the heaviest plating of the eight, and the same dead organ under it. Nothing about the armour helps: the hive isn't looking for a shape, it's listening for a signal that never comes.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.donut.name: Donut
ss.char.donut.description: Sealed survivor built around a hole — the shell closed into a ring where the emitter chamber used to be, so this one didn't just go quiet, it grew over the wound. The dead organ sits on the rim, off to one side.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.dot.name: Dot
ss.char.dot.description: A survivor of the same brood as everything hunting you — same antennae, same organ, same socket in the shell. The organ is `dead`: no halo, no bloom, a hairline crack across cold grey. That silence is the entire premise, and every one of the eight characters wears it in the same place. Dot is the sealed sphere: nothing leaks out of it at all.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.egg.name: Egg
ss.char.egg.description: Sealed survivor, and the one the fiction is least kind to — an unhatched shell that was never given a signal to lose. Same dead organ, same dead feelers; on this one they were dead from the start.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.hex.name: Hex
ss.char.hex.description: Sealed survivor in cell-shaped plating — the same hexagon the hive builds with, worn by something the hive no longer counts. Dead organ, dead feelers, six flat sides that fit nowhere any more.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.hourglass.name: Hourglass
ss.char.hourglass.description: Sealed survivor pinched at the waist — two chambers joined by a throat that nothing passes through any more. Same dead organ, same dead feelers as the other seven.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.prism.name: Prism
ss.char.prism.description: Sealed survivor cut to a hard facet — the only one of the eight whose shell catches light on two planes at once. Underneath it is the same dead organ as the rest.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.char.tri.name: Tri
ss.char.tri.description: Sealed survivor, wedge-shelled and pointed the way it runs. Same dead organ and dead feelers as the rest of the eight — the shape is the only thing that tells them apart, because none of them has anything to say.

idle.description: the shell holds its breath; the dead feelers keep sweeping for a signal that never comes

ss.enemy.bat.name: Drifter
ss.enemy.bat.description: Released from a vent to sweep for you. Two pale wings held back over a small dark body, with an organ underneath leaking the trail that tells the ground castes where you were. The wings carry the whole read — a wide bright horizontal against the Tracker's compact blob.

elite.description: A marked scout: brighter membranes, a heavier sting and a fatter trail.

flit.description: wings beat out of phase, body rocks under them

ss.enemy.boss.name: Chorus
ss.enemy.boss.description: Not the biggest thing in the hive — the loudest. A seated mass of carapace ringed by six organs that fire in sequence, so the light travels around it like a voice going round a room; that rotation is the whole read. Under the plates is a ring of husk teeth around a vent that has never eaten anything, only shouted. Gameplay slot unchanged (5:00 / 10:00 boss); body radius still ~38.

enraged.description: Phase two: the shell splits along every seam, the vent burns through, and the sequence collapses into all six organs screaming at once.

chorus.description: the light travels the ring — six organs firing in sequence, plates counter-rotating under them

ss.enemy.brazier.name: Signal stalk
ss.enemy.brazier.description: Not a creature — a relay. The hive grows these to repeat a scent across a level, which is why smashing one buys you quiet ground. A chitin stalk on a splayed root, a bulb organ at the top, and wisps going up where everything can smell them. The `spent` variant is the destroyed state: cracked stalk, dead bulb, no wisp.

spent.description: Smashed. The relay is dark, the cup is split and this stretch of hive has gone deaf — which is exactly why you broke it.

broadcast.description: the bulb swells on a slow cycle and the wisp climbs

ss.enemy.brute.name: Soldier
ss.enemy.brute.description: The caste that gets sent when a Tracker's call is answered. One heavy plated dome, two shearing mandibles and a pair of organs broadcasting the kill order. Big, bright and almost featureless on purpose — the tank has to read as mass from across the screen, so it is a slab of chitin rather than a study of one.

elite.description: A war caste: bleached plates, a spined ridge and a third organ. When this one broadcasts, the level turns around.

stomp.description: slow heavy gait, plates settling a beat behind the shell

ss.enemy.charger.name: Lance
ss.enemy.charger.description: Winds up in place, then crosses the gap faster than you can turn. A swept ember dart that reads as 'about to move fast' — drawn facing +x, the game flips it. Faithful port of the hand-drawn e_charger. Gameplay radius 10.

ss.enemy.imp.name: Tracker
ss.enemy.imp.description: The hive's first responder — the one that found you. One bright chitin body, a dark maw at the front, two thick feelers and a lit organ on its back. Deliberately not an insect: at four hundred on screen you read a shape and a glow, not anatomy, so head and thorax are fused and the legs are three stubs. Gameplay slot unchanged (fast, weak melee chaser); body radius still 8.5.

elite.description: Marked by the hive: bleached shell, a heavier maw and a brighter organ.

scuttle.description: legs cycle out of phase, body bobs, feelers sweep

ss.enemy.shot.name: Gland bolt
ss.enemy.shot.description: The Gland's spit — an acidic teal bolt with a soft glow, drawn pointing +x and rotated by the game to its heading. Faithful port of the hand-drawn e_shot (canvas grew 14→16 wide for the grid; geometry unchanged).

ss.enemy.skeleton.name: Molt
ss.enemy.skeleton.description: Nobody is inside. A shed carapace split down the front, held upright only by the signal rattling around in it. Cold pale grey where the Husk is warm bone, and the split is the whole silhouette: one bright shell with a dark seam of nothing lit from within.

elite.description: The shell answered louder than it should have — the seam forced wide open, and the signal inside is no longer faint.

rattle.description: the two halves breathe apart and the light between them swells

ss.enemy.spitter.name: Gland
ss.enemy.spitter.description: Ranged sac that holds the far edge of your reach and spits where you're going to be. A bulbous teal body with a firing snout on the right — drawn facing +x, the game flips it. Faithful port of the hand-drawn e_spitter (canvas grew 27→28 wide for the grid; geometry unchanged). Gameplay radius 11.

ss.enemy.zombie.name: Husk
ss.enemy.zombie.description: A drone that ran out of scent and stopped being anybody — the hive grafted an organ onto its chest and it walks again. Bleached bone, slumped forward, one arm hanging longer than the other. Tall and pale where the Tracker is low and amber: at a glance you are reading height and value, not detail.

elite.description: The hive doubled down: a fresh fully lit graft in the shoulder beside the dying one in the chest.

shamble.description: heavy lopsided gait — the long arm swings a beat behind the legs

ss.env.antenna.name: Watcher antenna
ss.env.antenna.description: A feeler the size of the screen, meant to stand just off the corner of the home screen and sweep the air over it. Everything else in the roster wears antennae at body scale; this one is drawn at menu scale, so whatever is carrying it is enormous and off-frame — which is the point on a title screen for a run about being hunted by smell. Silhouette only, and unlit like every antenna in this world, because a glow would mean emission and an antenna only ever receives. The root sits on the document origin, so a scene places it by saying where it comes out of the floor.

twitch.description: one snap, a recoil and a settle, travelling root to tip — the ordinary tic, fired on an irregular beat by whoever is playing it

shiver.description: the whole feeler buzzes at once, swelling and dying, the shudder running up its length — saved for after a skipped beat, so it reads as a reaction rather than a habit

flinch.description: snatched away in a single frame and crept back over the rest — for when something touches it

ss.env.ground.name: Hive ground (SS)
ss.env.ground.description: Feelers' 128px ground tile: dark iron-red dirt. Warm enough to read as earth rather than void, dark enough that the hive's magenta still has somewhere to go — the ambient screen stays calm and event pulses do the shouting. No checker: the 32px grid read as tiling rather than as ground, so the floor is now plain dirt with burrow pits and rust flecks where old scent trails dried. Hand-listed pit and fleck coordinates are kept verbatim from the original makeGround, so the tile stays pixel-stable.

ss.env.menu.name: Home screen — under the soil
ss.env.menu.description: Not a view of the hive but a place inside it: packed earth seen from within. Six sedimentary bands settle from the top of the frame to the bottom, and every one is a translucent wash over a single dark base rather than its own colour — that is what keeps them a whisper apart instead of stripes. Scent is the only thing moving through the ground: pheromone bleeding along the seams where one layer met another, pooling under the denser bands, threading down old root channels, and rising in slow motes. No creatures, no structures, no horizon; the picture is the ground itself. The middle bands are the flattest and quietest because the title, cast row and buttons sit there. Authored at 1280x720 so the menu's cover-scale does not magnify it.

seep.description: nothing here moves but the smell — motes climb through the layers and the seams breathe

ss.fx.gust.name: Gust
ss.fx.gust.description: Air dragged along behind Dancing Mandibles. Three curved streaks of different length, none of them closed and none of them concentric — a closed ring reads as a shockwave, and this is supposed to read as the room being pulled after something.

ss.fx.impact.name: Shell break
ss.fx.impact.description: What it looks like when your weapon lands: chitin splitting, not blood. A hard cold flash and four shell chips thrown outward — deliberately frost-white so player damage never gets confused with the hive's magenta broadcast. Spawn it at the contact point.

play.description: snap out, chips fly, gone in a fifth of a second

ss.fx.pickup.name: Borrowed signal
ss.fx.pickup.description: Absorbing a scent crystal — the only moment in the run when the player has a voice. A magenta bloom rises out of the pickup point, flares, and dies within half a second, and it is the one place the hive's colour is allowed to touch the player. Playing this on every XP pickup is what makes the dead organ on the character mean something.

play.description: a voice for half a second, then nothing again

ss.fx.punch.name: Puncture
ss.fx.punch.description: What a pierced body leaves behind for an instant: a hole with its edge lit and four short splinters thrown out along the line of travel. Marks the moment a shot went through rather than stopped, which is the whole difference the evolution buys.

ss.icon.amount.name: Amount icon
ss.icon.amount.description: Passive icon: two white dots side by side — one more of everything. Port of the hand-drawn i_amount from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.area.name: Area icon
ss.icon.area.description: Passive icon: a bright inner circle and a fainter outer one — reach spreading outward. Port of the hand-drawn i_area from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.armor.name: Armor icon
ss.icon.armor.description: Passive icon: pale steel shield — a flat plate over a point. Port of the hand-drawn i_armor from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.banish.name: Banish icon
ss.icon.banish.description: Shop icon: coral X, two heavy crossed strokes. Port of the hand-drawn i_banish from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.boomerang.name: Mandible icon
ss.icon.boomerang.description: UI slot icon for the paired mandibles, composing `ss.proj.boom` via `use`. Third of the weapon icons to be derived from its projectile instead of hand-drawn a second time — the original BootScene authored five weapon shapes twice, with independently tuned coordinates.

ss.icon.card.name: Ricochet Spine icon
ss.icon.card.description: UI slot icon for the Ricochet Spine. Composes `ss.proj.card` via `use`, tilted the way the wand icon tilts its dart, so the slot shows the wing membrane itself instead of the old hand-drawn i_card (white rounded rect, red pip).

evolved.description: Gold-rimmed evolved twin (the old i_card_evo), derived rather than drawn again.

ss.icon.cooldown.name: Cooldown icon
ss.icon.cooldown.description: Passive icon: frost hourglass, two triangles meeting point-to-point. Port of the hand-drawn i_cooldown from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.curse.name: Curse icon
ss.icon.curse.description: Meta powerup icon: arcane imp face — round head, dark eyes, two hanging fangs. Port of the hand-drawn i_curse from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.drone.name: Broodling icon
ss.icon.drone.description: UI slot icon for the broodling. Composes `ss.proj.drone` via `use` so the hatchling in the slot is the hatchling on screen, replacing the old hand-drawn i_drone (flat hexagon, navy core). Rim keeps the original's aqua.

evolved.description: Gold-rimmed evolved twin (the old i_drone_evo), derived rather than drawn again.

ss.icon.duration.name: Duration icon
ss.icon.duration.description: Passive icon: a lavender clock face, hands at ten past. The hands are thin rects standing in for the original's line strokes. Port of the hand-drawn i_duration from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.food.name: Food icon
ss.icon.food.description: Shop icon: chitin-brown loaf with a pale bone crumb at its edge. A separate drawing from the `ss.pickup.food` world pickup — this is the shop's shorthand, not the item. Port of the hand-drawn i_food from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.frost.name: Chirp icon
ss.icon.frost.description: UI slot icon for Chirp, the expanding wave. The one weapon icon that does not compose its projectile: `ss.proj.ring` is a 128px wash of near-transparent bands, and at a sixth scale it dissolves to nothing. The glyph instead draws the same idea — an expanding ring, a fainter one behind it — at icon weight. Port of the hand-drawn i_frost.

ss.icon.greed.name: Greed icon
ss.icon.greed.description: Meta powerup icon: gold coin with a pale slot gleam down the middle. Port of the hand-drawn i_greed from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.growth.name: Growth icon
ss.icon.growth.description: Meta powerup icon: frost up-arrow, head over stem. Port of the hand-drawn i_growth from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.luck.name: Luck icon
ss.icon.luck.description: Passive icon: four-leaf clover — four venom circles and a darker stem. Port of the hand-drawn i_luck from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.magnet.name: Magnet icon (SS)
ss.icon.magnet.description: Shape Survivors passive icon: pink horseshoe magnet — an arc arch with two leg rects. Port of i_magnet (BootScene.ts:607-613).

ss.icon.maxhp.name: Max HP icon
ss.icon.maxhp.description: Passive icon: coral heart built the classic way, two lobes over a point. Port of the hand-drawn i_maxhp from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.might.name: Might icon (SS)
ss.icon.might.description: Shape Survivors passive icon: coral up-arrow (triangle + stem). Port of i_might (BootScene.ts:574-576).

ss.icon.mine.name: Spore icon
ss.icon.mine.description: UI slot icon for Spore, the cache dropper. Composes `ss.proj.mine` itself via `use` — the cache the icon promises is the cache the ground shows — replacing the old hand-drawn i_mine (grey disc, red core). Rim keeps that original's red: the slot color the HUD taught players to read as 'trap'.

evolved.description: Gold-rimmed evolved twin (the old i_mine_evo), derived rather than drawn again.

ss.icon.movespeed.name: Move speed icon
ss.icon.movespeed.description: Passive icon: a single pale-aqua arrowhead aimed right. Port of the hand-drawn i_movespeed from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.pendulum.name: Chained Head icon
ss.icon.pendulum.description: UI slot icon for the Chained Head. Composes `ss.proj.ball` via `use` so the slot shows the actual packed head-plate, replacing the old hand-drawn i_pendulum (grey line and ball). Rim keeps the original's steel.

evolved.description: Gold-rimmed evolved twin (the old i_pendulum_evo), derived rather than drawn again.

ss.icon.pocket.name: Pocket icon
ss.icon.pocket.description: Meta powerup icon for the relic pocket: a drawstring pouch, flared mouth over a round body, cinched dark across the neck. Port of the hand-drawn i_pocket from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.recovery.name: Recovery icon
ss.icon.recovery.description: Passive icon: venom green plus sign, two crossed bars. Port of the hand-drawn i_recovery from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.reroll.name: Reroll icon
ss.icon.reroll.description: Shop icon: venom refresh arrow — a three-quarter arc with an arrowhead at its start. Port of the hand-drawn i_reroll from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.revival.name: Revival icon
ss.icon.revival.description: Meta powerup icon: bright gold lightning bolt, three overlapping triangles. Port of the hand-drawn i_revival from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.skip.name: Skip icon
ss.icon.skip.description: Shop icon: pale double chevron skipping forward. Port of the hand-drawn i_skip from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.speed.name: Attack speed icon
ss.icon.speed.description: Passive icon: double chevron pointing right, venom green. Port of the hand-drawn i_speed from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.icon.wand.name: Shell dart icon
ss.icon.wand.description: UI slot icon for the dart thrower. The glyph is not a second drawing of the weapon — it composes `ss.proj.bolt` itself via `use`, so the icon can never drift from the projectile the way the original i_wand and p_bolt did. Evolved is a rim swap, not a redraw.

evolved.description: Gold-rimmed evolved twin (the old i_wand_evo), derived rather than drawn again.

ss.icon.whip.name: Lash icon
ss.icon.whip.description: UI slot icon for the mandible lash. Composes the real `ss.proj.slash` arc via `use` at a quarter scale, so retuning the weapon's sweep restyles its icon in the same edit.

ss.lib.antenna.name: Scent antenna
ss.lib.antenna.description: Tapered feeler rooted at the origin, curving up and forward (+x), tipped with a sensing nub. The hive reads the world with these instead of eyes — which is why nothing in the enemy roster has any. Deliberately unlit: in this world a glow means emission, never sensing, so only organs light up and an antenna can never be mistaken for an eye.

dead.description: A survivor's antenna — intact, but nothing on the air to read.

ss.lib.eye.name: SS shared eye
ss.lib.eye.description: Shape Survivors' single direction-reading eye dot, shared by all 8 characters (BootScene.ts:112). Compose with `use` at [5, eyeY-14].

ss.lib.organ.name: Pheromone organ
ss.lib.organ.description: The premise of the game in one part. Every creature in the hive carries this scent organ, lit — it is how they announce themselves and how they are recognized. The player carries the same organ in the same place, `dead`: cracked, unlit, silent. That is why they are hunted. Composed everywhere via `use`, so the whole roster shares one definition.

dead.description: The player's organ: no halo, no bloom, a hairline crack across a cold grey bulb. The silence that gets you chased.

faint.description: A dying signal — husks and spent stalks. Lit, but barely.

pulse.description: the scent broadcast — a slow swell

ss.lib.wisp.name: Scent wisp
ss.lib.wisp.description: Pheromone leaking upward — three blobs thinning as they rise. Marks anything that is broadcasting: stalks, vents, and the trail a flier leaves behind. The player never has one.

rise.description: blobs drift up and thin out, staggered

ss.pickup.chest.name: Brood cell
ss.pickup.chest.description: A sealed hexagonal cell the hive built and forgot. Prying one open is the only time in the run you are the thing doing the opening. Capped with wax, ribbed with chitin, and faintly lit from inside — something in there is still signalling. The cell is stretched along its flat axis, which is what separates it from the coin: the coin is the one other hexagon on the floor, and it is regular. Stretching rather than scaling keeps every slanted edge at its comb angle, so the shape still belongs to the hive's architecture.

cursed.description: This one was not forgotten. The cap is dark, the seam is split, and whatever is inside answered when the hive called.

tease.description: the cap flexes as something inside pushes at it, and the seam flexes with it

ss.pickup.coin.name: Chitin shard
ss.pickup.coin.description: Currency, of a sort. A polished disc of shell — the hive trades in material, not metal, and a clean plate off a Soldier is worth carrying out. Gold-warm so it never gets confused with the near-white scent crystals.

spin.description: catches the light as it turns

ss.pickup.food.name: Gland
ss.pickup.food.description: A nutrient sac cut out of something that stopped needing it. Warm, soft-shelled and slightly translucent against everything else's chitin — the only round soft thing in the level, which is exactly why it reads as heal at a glance.

ss.pickup.gem.name: Scent crystal
ss.pickup.gem.description: What a hive creature leaves behind when it dies: its signal, crystallized. You pick them up because each one is a piece of the voice you lost — which is why they count as experience. Deliberately kept near-white and neutral: the game tints this sprite per XP tier at runtime, so any hue baked in here would fight the tint.

bob.description: hovers and breathes — it is still, faintly, saying something

ss.proj.aura.name: Blast disc
ss.proj.aura.description: The shared area-of-effect wash every explosive weapon spawns. Two hard constraints keep this one plain: the weapon code scales it by `r / 64`, and it is tinted per weapon at runtime — so every fill here is neutral white, exactly as in the original. Any hue baked in would fight the tint, the same reason the scent crystal stays colourless.

play.description: core collapses as the rim runs out

ss.proj.ball.name: Chained head
ss.proj.ball.description: A Soldier's head-plate packed solid and swung on a cord. Heavy, ridged, and about as far from subtle as this arsenal gets. Its geometry is load-bearing: the weapon code scales this sprite by `ballR / 14`, so the 28px canvas and ~13.5 body radius must stay as they are.

ss.proj.bolt.name: Shell dart
ss.proj.bolt.description: A chip of molt shell knapped to a point and thrown, lit cold along the edge. Points +x, which is the direction the weapon code rotates it to. Acid Rain's variant runs pink instead — the one that hunts is the one that carries your scent.

evolved.description: Acid Rain's dart: the same shell, wet with the scent it is following. Pink where the thrown one is cold — a bolt that turns is a bolt that knows where you want it, and that has to read at a glance from the ones that just fly straight.

fly.description: the streak stutters as it travels

ss.proj.boom.name: Paired mandibles
ss.proj.boom.description: Two Soldier mandibles bound at the elbow so they come back to you. The concave chevron silhouette is kept from the original boomerang — it reads at any rotation, which matters for a thing that spins the whole time it is airborne. No spin animation is declared here on purpose: whole-body rotation is the engine's job (the weapon code already does `sprite.rotation += spin * dt`), and a document animation can only move parts within the body.

ss.proj.card.name: Wing blade
ss.proj.card.description: A Drifter's wing membrane stretched taut on a bone frame and thrown edge-first — the veins are still in it. Of the whole arsenal this is the one that most obviously used to be alive, which is the point.

evolved.description: Marked Deck's ace: the membrane cured to gold leaf and a spade burned into it, point up. A wing that has been made into a card rather than a card that was always one — the bone frame and the spine are still there under the gilding.

ss.proj.chip.name: Shell chip
ss.proj.chip.description: A splinter the orbiter sheds when it fires — the same hexagon it is, an eighth the size and still cold. Its whole job is to not be mistaken for the dart you throw, so it keeps the drone's grey and none of the violet.

evolved.description: Sentinel Drone's chip, driven hard enough to go through. Nearly twice the size of the one it grew from and lit rather than grey — a shot that pierces has to be findable on a dark floor, and the unevolved chip is deliberately small enough to lose.

ss.proj.drone.name: Shell orbiter
ss.proj.drone.description: A hexagonal plate cut from a Molt and set spinning around you on nothing but momentum. The hive builds in hexagons, so this is quite literally a piece of their architecture turned into a weapon — the same cold grey as the shell it came from.

hum.description: the cut cell turns inside a plate that does not

ss.proj.mine.name: Spore pod
ss.proj.mine.description: A hollowed spore case packed with whatever was left and set down to wait. Its fuse light is deliberately cold: in this world a magenta glow means something is calling to the hive, and the last thing you want from your own trap is for it to advertise you.

armed.description: the fuse ticks — cold, quiet, and not on the hive's frequency

ss.proj.ring.name: Frost nova
ss.proj.ring.description: The one thing in the arsenal that isn't scavenged — cold thrown outward in a ring, the survivor's own answer to being surrounded. Three concentric bands and nothing else: the weapon code scales this sprite by `wave.r / 62`, so anything with a shape of its own is blown up with it, and the studs that used to sit on the rim arrived on screen as gems stuck to a hoop. Geometry is load-bearing — the 128px canvas and the 60px rim radius must not move. Kept near-white so any runtime tint still reads.

play.description: the rim snaps outward and the wash follows it out

ss.proj.scanline.name: Scanline tile (SS)
ss.proj.scanline.description: Shape Survivors CRT scanline tile: one 4×2 dark row in a 4×4 tile, tiled full-screen by the HUD. Port of scanline (BootScene.ts:448-453).

ss.proj.slash.name: Lash sweep
ss.proj.slash.description: The whip is a Soldier's mandible on a cord, so its arc is a bone crescent with a honed frost edge on the leading side and a thinner echo trailing behind it. Nothing about it glows — it is hive material with the signal stripped out. Canvas and anchor unchanged from the original `slash` texture so the weapon code's spawn offsets still land.

recover.description: the stroke coming back up. The lash is already spent, so the body is thinner and the honed edge is nearly gone; what's left is the trail — a longer, brighter echo where the tip has just been. Same canvas and anchor as the base, so the weapon code can swap textures without moving anything.

play.description: the edge outruns the body, then both go

ss.terrain.arch.name: Broken arch (SS)
ss.terrain.arch.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a standing gateway with its keystone gone — two jambs and the broken springing stones where the arch used to close. Symmetric, so each side is one part mirrored. Port of t_arch from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.arrow.name: Compass arrow (SS)
ss.terrain.arrow.description: Shape Survivors HUD compass toward active ruins, pointing +x. Port of arrow (BootScene.ts:325-331).

ss.terrain.boulder.name: Spore boulder (SS)
ss.terrain.boulder.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: mossy boulder with glowing soul-green spore pits. Port of t_boulder (BootScene.ts:230-239).

ss.terrain.chitin.name: Chitin slab (SS)
ss.terrain.chitin.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a broken slab of hive carapace, ridged amber, leaning out of the ground. The three ridges are thin rects standing in for the original's line strokes. Port of t_chitin from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.fungi.name: Glow fungi (SS)
ss.terrain.fungi.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: three glowing mushroom caps on pale stems. Port of t_fungi (BootScene.ts:277-290) — the original's shroom() closure becomes three part clusters.

ss.terrain.husk.name: Bleached husk (SS)
ss.terrain.husk.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: the bleached dome of something that ran out of scent — a half-shell of nested ribs sitting on the ground line. Arcs are ring parts swept 180→360 (the top half). Port of t_husk from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.pillar.name: Broken pillar (SS)
ss.terrain.pillar.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a broken column of cut stone — lit down one side, two drum joints, a snapped capital riding the top. Masonry maps to the $smoke ramp (the ruins' standing stones keep $carapace; this stone is cut, not grown). Port of t_pillar from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.rubble.name: Masonry rubble (SS)
ss.terrain.rubble.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: three scattered chips of the same cut masonry as the pillar and slab. Port of t_rubble from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.ruins.name: Sunken ruin ring (SS)
ss.terrain.ruins.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a sunken stone ring humming with old scent — a glowing pheromone core in a dark bowl, three broken standing stones around the rim. Port of t_ruins from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.slab.name: Toppled slab (SS)
ss.terrain.slab.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a toppled wall block or altar stone — lit top face, two block seams cut through it. Port of t_slab from Feelers' BootScene.

ss.terrain.spire.name: Pheromone spire (SS)
ss.terrain.spire.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: crystallized pheromone trail — a pink crystal cluster with glow tip and ground shadow. Port of t_spire (BootScene.ts:217-229).

ss.terrain.vent.name: Pheromone vent (SS)
ss.terrain.vent.description: Shape Survivors set dressing: a fumarole crater mound exhaling pheromone — three pink wisps rising and fading. Port of t_vent from Feelers' BootScene.

tile.ground.name: Ground tile
tile.ground.description: Tileable 32px floor: two-tone checker with seeded pebble and speck scatter. Deterministic — the same seed always yields the same scatter, so renders are diffable.

weapon.boomerang.name: Boomerang
weapon.boomerang.description: Bone chevron throwing blade with a steel rivet — a concave silhouette. Single source of truth: the icon composes this same document via `use`.
